question: According to the census data, which Union Territory of India recorded the highest population density in 2011? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Puducherry
Delhi
Chandigarh
Lakshadweep
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Delhi

Explanation:
According to the 2011 Census, Delhi recorded the highest population density among all Union Territories of India, with 11,320 persons per square kilometer. Delhi is a National Capital Territory and its high density is due to rapid urbanization and migration. Other Union Territories like Chandigarh (9,258), Puducherry (2,598), and Lakshadweep (2,013) have lower densities. It is notable that Delhi is also the most densely populated state/UT in India overall.

question: Which of the following is not a component of the core infrastructure sectors of India (as per the Index of Eight Core Industries)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following was a major fiscal reform introduced in India as part of the 1991 economic reforms? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Introduction of GST
Introduction of the Modified Value Added Tax
Abolition of wealth tax
Implementation of the FRBM Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Introduction of the Modified Value Added Tax

Explanation:
As part of the 1991 economic reforms, India implemented several fiscal measures to control the fiscal deficit and boost revenue. One key reform was the introduction and expansion of the Modified Value Added Tax (MODVAT), which was initially introduced in 1986 but significantly strengthened during the 1991 reforms. MODVAT allowed credit for excise duties, making the tax system more efficient. The GST was implemented later in 2017. The FRBM Act was passed in 2003. The abolition of wealth tax occurred in 2015. Thus, MODVAT is closely associated with the 1991 reforms.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Full form of MODVAT → Modified Value Added Tax
☛ When was MODVAT introduced? → 1986
☛ Main objectives of 1991 reforms → Reduce fiscal deficit and liberalize the economy
☛ When was GST implemented? → 1 July 2017
☛ Purpose of FRBM Act → Ensure fiscal discipline
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 1991 के आर्थिक सुधारों के भाग के रूप में भारत में शुरू किया गया एक प्रमुख राजकोषीय सुधार था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संशोधित मूल्य वर्धित कर का परिचय

Explanation:
1991 के आर्थिक सुधारों के तहत, भारत ने राजकोषीय घाटे को नियंत्रित करने और राजस्व बढ़ाने के लिए कई उपाय किए। इनमें से एक प्रमुख सुधार संशोधित मूल्य वर्धित कर (MODVAT) की शुरुआत थी, जिसे 1986 में पेश किया गया था लेकिन 1991 के सुधारों के दौरान इसका विस्तार और सुदृढ़ीकरण किया गया। MODVAT प्रणाली ने उत्पाद शुल्क में क्रेडिट की अनुमति देकर कर प्रणाली को अधिक कुशल बनाया। GST बाद में 2017 में लागू हुआ। FRBM अधिनियम 2003 में पारित हुआ। धन कर का उन्मूलन 2015 में किया गया था। इसलिए, MODVAT 1991 के सुधारों से निकटता से जुड़ा है।

question: Which index combines life expectancy, education and per capita income to measure a country’s human development?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: GDP per capita
Human Development Index (HDI)
Consumer Price Index
Gini Index
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Human Development Index (HDI)

Explanation:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is based on three dimensions: life expectancy (health), education (years of schooling and expected years), and per capita income (standard of living). This index measures a country's overall human development, not just economic growth. HDI value ranges from 0 to 1, where 1 indicates highest development. It provides a broader perspective on human well-being rather than focusing solely on income.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who releases HDI? → UNDP
☛ What are the three dimensions of HDI? → Life expectancy, education, per capita income
☛ What is the range of HDI values? → 0 to 1
☛ Which country has the highest HDI in the world? → Switzerland (2022)
☛ Which country has the lowest HDI in the world? → Somalia (2022)
question_hi: कौन सा सूचकांक किसी देश के मानव विकास को मापने के लिए जीवन प्रत्याशा, शिक्षा और प्रति व्यक्ति आय को जोड़ता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: प्रति व्यक्ति GDP
मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI)
उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक
गिनी सूचकांक
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI)

Explanation:
मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) संयुक्त राष्ट्र विकास कार्यक्रम (UNDP) द्वारा जारी किया जाता है। यह तीन आयामों पर आधारित है: जीवन प्रत्याशा (स्वास्थ्य), शिक्षा (स्कूली शिक्षा के वर्ष और अपेक्षित वर्ष), और प्रति व्यक्ति आय (जीवन स्तर)। यह सूचकांक किसी देश के समग्र मानव विकास को मापता है, न कि केवल आर्थिक विकास को। HDI का मान 0 से 1 के बीच होता है, जहां 1 उच्चतम विकास को दर्शाता है। यह केवल आय पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने के बजाय मानव कल्याण का व्यापक दृष्टिकोण प्रदान करता है।

question: Which state / union territory had the highest urbanisation in 2011, as per the Census of India data?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)

question: What three-part economic strategy defined India’s policy changes in the 1990s?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation
Urbanisation, Industrialisation and Digitalisation
Nationalisation, Regulation and Protectionism
Devolution, Decentralisation and Deregulation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation

Explanation:
After the 1991 economic crisis, the Indian government adopted a new economic policy known as the LPG model. It consisted of three pillars: Liberalisation (removing license raj and controls), Privatisation (reducing the role of the public sector and promoting private enterprise), and Globalisation (opening the economy to international trade and investment). This policy transformed India from a closed economy to a market-oriented one. The reforms were implemented by Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao. The strategy aimed to accelerate economic growth, attract foreign investment, and increase competitiveness.

☛ Architect of 1991 economic reforms → Dr. Manmohan Singh
☛ Prime Minister during reforms → P.V. Narasimha Rao
☛ Main objective of Liberalisation → Abolish license raj
☛ Effect of Globalisation → Increase in foreign investment and trade
question_hi: 1990 के दशक में भारत की नीतिगत परिवर्तनों को किस तीन-भाग वाली आर्थिक रणनीति ने परिभाषित किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण

Explanation:
1991 के आर्थिक संकट के बाद भारत सरकार ने एक नई आर्थिक नीति अपनाई, जिसे LPG मॉडल कहा जाता है। इसमें तीन प्रमुख स्तंभ शामिल थे: उदारीकरण (लाइसेंस राज और नियंत्रणों को समाप्त करना), निजीकरण (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की भूमिका कम करना और निजी क्षेत्र को बढ़ावा देना), और वैश्वीकरण (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार और निवेश के लिए अर्थव्यवस्था को खोलना)। इस नीति ने भारत को बंद अर्थव्यवस्था से खुली बाजार अर्थव्यवस्था में बदल दिया। वित्त मंत्री डॉ. मनमोहन सिंह ने प्रधानमंत्री पी.वी. नरसिम्हा राव के नेतृत्व में इन सुधारों को लागू किया। इस रणनीति का उद्देश्य आर्थिक विकास को गति देना, विदेशी निवेश आकर्षित करना और प्रतिस्पर्धा बढ़ाना था।

question: Why is infrastructure referred to as the 'wheels' of economic growth?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: It is part of international trade.
It supports currency circulation.
It enables delivery of goods, services and access.
It helps in stabilising inflation.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It enables delivery of goods, services and access.

Explanation:
Infrastructure such as roads, railways, ports, electricity, and telecommunications provides the foundational framework for the economy. It enables the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, thereby driving economic activities. It is called the 'wheels' because it provides mobility to the economy, just as wheels propel a vehicle. Hence, infrastructure is a key factor in accelerating economic growth.

question: Human development emphasises enlarging people’s choices by improving health, education, and income. Which global organisation publishes the Human Development Index (HDI)?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: United Nations Development Programme
International Monetary Fund
World Bank
World Economic Forum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is United Nations Development Programme

Explanation:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is a socio-economic measure that ranks countries based on life expectancy, education, and per capita income. It was first developed in 1990 by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes it in its annual Human Development Report. The core objective of HDI is to expand people's choices and emphasize the human dimensions of economic growth. UNDP is a global network of the United Nations working for poverty eradication and sustainable development.

question: What was the major aim of India’s 1991 economic reforms? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: To reduce taxes on luxury goods
To stabilise India’s economy
To nationalise all companies
To increase government control
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To stabilise India's economy

Explanation:
The major aim of India's 1991 economic reforms was to stabilise the economy, which faced a severe balance of payments crisis with foreign reserves dropping to only two weeks of imports. The reforms introduced liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation (LPG), ending the licence raj, promoting foreign investment, and reducing import tariffs. These market-oriented policies stabilized the economy, led to higher growth rates, and laid the foundation for long-term development. The crisis prompted the government to adopt structural adjustments and fiscal discipline, ultimately transforming India into one of the fastest-growing economies in the world.

☛ What was India's growth rate after the 1991 reforms? → Around 6-7% per annum

question: Which of the following is not true in regard to the exchange rate of Indian Rupee ? (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Mainly, its price is in terms of US Dollar.
It is decided by Reserve Bank of India.
It is published by Reserve bank of India.
It is decided by market forces.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is decided by Reserve Bank of India

Explanation:
In India, the exchange rate of the rupee is determined by market forces of demand and supply, not by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The RBI does not fix the exchange rate; it may intervene occasionally to manage volatility. Thus, this statement is incorrect. The price of the rupee is mainly quoted in terms of the US dollar, and the RBI publishes the reference rate. Since the economic reforms of 1991, India has adopted a floating exchange rate system, where the rate is largely market-determined.

question: What is Net National Product (NNP)? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: NNP = GNP - Depreciation
NNP = GDP = Income from abroad
NNP = GNP + Depreciation
NNP = GDP - Income from abroad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NNP = GNP - Depreciation

Explanation:
Net National Product (NNP) is the total value of all final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country in a year, after deducting depreciation. It is obtained by subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP). Depreciation represents the decline in the value of capital goods due to wear and tear or obsolescence. NNP can be measured at market prices (NNP at MP) and factor cost (National Income). It includes net factor income from abroad but excludes depreciation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is National Income at factor cost called? → National Income
☛ What is another name for depreciation? → Capital Consumption Allowance
☛ What is the difference between GNP and NNP? → GNP includes depreciation, NNP does not.
☛ What does NNP at market prices include? → Net Indirect Taxes (NIT)
☛ Who calculates National Income in India? → National Statistical Office (NSO)

Explanation:
निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (NNP) किसी देश के नागरिकों द्वारा किसी वर्ष में उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य है, जिसमें से मूल्यह्रास घटा दिया जाता है। यह सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) से मूल्यह्रास को घटाकर प्राप्त किया जाता है। मूल्यह्रास पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के टूट-फूट या अप्रचलन के कारण उनके मूल्य में कमी को दर्शाता है। NNP को बाजार कीमतों (NNP at MP) और कारक लागत (국민소득) दोनों पर मापा जा सकता है। यह विदेशों से शुद्ध कारक आय को भी शामिल करता है, लेकिन मूल्यह्रास को नहीं।

question: The "Indradhanush” framework, an Indian government initiative, is for: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: resource mobilisation
revamping of Public Sector Banks
revamping of Private Sector Banks
capacity building in Private Sector Banks
solution:

The Indradhanush framework is an initiative of the Government of India for the revamping of Public Sector Banks (PSBs). It was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Finance. question: Which of the following bodies recommends minimum support price for crops? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: NITI Ayog
NABARD
CACP
FCI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is CACP

Explanation:
The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommends the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops in India. CACP is a statutory body under the Ministry of Agriculture. It considers factors like production cost, market prices, and farmers' income before recommending MSP. Established in 1965, CACP's recommendations are approved by the central government, and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) procures crops at MSP. NABARD deals with agricultural finance, while NITI Ayog aids in policy formulation. Thus, CACP is the correct body for MSP recommendations.

question: During which five year plan did India opt for a mixed economy? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Fourth Five Year Plan
Second Five Year Plan
Third Five Year Plan
First Five Year Plan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Second Five Year Plan

Explanation:
India adopted the mixed economy model during the Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961). This plan emphasized the coexistence of public and private sectors. The Industrial Policy of 1956 formalized this model by categorizing industries into three schedules: Schedule A (state monopoly), Schedule B (mixed), and Schedule C (private). The plan was based on the Mahalanobis model, which focused on heavy industries. The mixed economy approach became the cornerstone of India's economic policy, balancing state control with private enterprise.

☛ What was the main objective of the Second Plan? → Development of heavy industries

☛ On whose model was the Second Plan based? → P.C. Mahalanobis
☛ What was the main focus of the First Plan? → Agriculture and irrigation

question: Jon Beel Mela is the only fair in India where barter system is still used. In which state does it take place? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/01/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following taxes/duties is NOT covered under GST? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 1)

Central excise duty
VAT
solution:

Explanation:

GST subsumes entertainment tax (now levied by local bodies), central excise duty (included in CGST), and VAT (included in SGST). question: Which of the following taxes is levied by the Union and collected and appropriated by the States? (RRB JE EE (01/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Estate Duty
Stamp Duty
Taxes on Newspapers
Passenger and Goods Tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Stamp Duty

Explanation:
Under Article 268 of the Indian Constitution, Stamp Duty is the tax that is levied by the Union government but collected and appropriated by the State governments. This tax is primarily imposed on legal documents such as bills, promissory notes, and other instruments. In contrast, Estate Duty is levied and collected by the Union but distributed to the states. Taxes on Newspapers are levied and collected by the Union, while Passenger and Goods Tax is levied by the states. Therefore, only Stamp Duty satisfies the condition of being levied by the Union and collected/appropriated by the states, making it the correct answer.

☛ Which taxes are levied and collected by Union? → Estate Duty and Taxes on Newspapers
☛ Which tax is levied by States? → Passenger and Goods Tax
☛ On what documents is Stamp Duty imposed? → Legal documents like bills and promissory notes
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कर संघ द्वारा लगाया जाता है और राज्यों द्वारा एकत्र और विनियोजित किया जाता है? (RRB JE EE (01/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options_hi: संपदा शुल्क
स्टाम्प शुल्क
समाचारपत्रों पर कर
यात्री एवं माल कर

Solution: सही उत्तर है स्टाम्प शुल्क

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 268 के तहत स्टाम्प शुल्क (Stamp Duty) वह कर है जिसे संघ सरकार द्वारा लगाया जाता है लेकिन इसका संग्रहण और विनियोजन राज्य सरकारों द्वारा किया जाता है। यह कर मुख्यतः वादपत्रों, बिलों और अन्य कानूनी दस्तावेजों पर लगता है। इसी प्रकार, संपदा शुल्क (Estate Duty) भी संघ द्वारा लगाया और एकत्र किया जाता है लेकिन इसे राज्यों को वितरित किया जाता है। समाचारपत्रों पर कर (Taxes on Newspapers) संघ द्वारा लगाया और एकत्र किया जाता है, जबकि यात्री एवं माल कर (Passenger and Goods Tax) राज्यों द्वारा लगाया जाता है। अतः प्रश्न में वर्णित शर्तों को केवल स्टाम्प शुल्क पूरा करता है।

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding GST? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: France is the first country to introduce GST.
July 1st is celebrated as GST day by the Central Board of Excise and Customs.
GST cannot be collected by the state government.
India has chosen Canada’s structure of dual GST.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GST cannot be collected by the state government.

Explanation:
GST is an indirect tax implemented in India on July 1, 2017. India follows a dual GST model, where both the central and state governments collect GST. The central government collects CGST (Central GST) and state governments collect SGST (State GST), so the statement that GST cannot be collected by state governments is false. France was the first country to introduce GST in 1954. In India, July 1 is celebrated as GST Day by the Central Board of Excise and Customs. India adopted Canada's dual GST structure, which imposes separate taxes at federal and provincial levels. Thus, option 3 is incorrect.

Explanation:
GST एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है जो भारत में 1 जुलाई 2017 से लागू हुआ। भारत ने दोहरी GST प्रणाली अपनाई है, जिसमें केंद्र और राज्य दोनों GST एकत्र करते हैं। केंद्र सरकार CGST (केंद्रीय GST) और राज्य सरकार SGST (राज्य GST) वसूलती है, इसलिए यह कथन गलत है कि राज्य सरकार GST एकत्र नहीं कर सकती। फ्रांस वास्तव में GST लागू करने वाला पहला देश था (1954 में)। भारत में केंद्रीय उत्पाद एवं सीमा शुल्क बोर्ड द्वारा 1 जुलाई को GST दिवस मनाया जाता है। भारत ने कनाडा की दोहरी GST संरचना को अपनाया, जहां केंद्र और राज्य दोनों अलग-अलग कर लगाते हैं। इस प्रकार, विकल्प 3 असत्य है।

question: What are the four tax rates in India under GST? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%
3%, 6%, 18% and 28%
6%, 12%, 17% and 28%
6%, 9%, 18% and 28%
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%

Explanation:
Under GST in India, there are four main tax slabs for goods and services: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. Additionally, essential items are taxed at 0%, and gold attracts a 3% rate. The 18% slab is the standard rate applied to most services and goods. The 28% slab is reserved for luxury and demerit items. There are no GST rates of 6%, 9%, or 17%. The correct option lists 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. Thus, Option 1 is correct.

question: The reduction in the external value of the domestic currency is called: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Economic growth
Devaluation of currency
Increase in purchasing power
Decrease in inflation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Devaluation of currency

Explanation:
When the external value of a country's currency (its value relative to other currencies) decreases, it is called devaluation of currency. This is usually done deliberately by the government or central bank to boost exports and make imports more expensive. However, it can lead to inflation. On the other hand, appreciation of currency refers to an increase in external value. Economic growth and purchasing power are not directly related to this concept.
